items.title: Solon Township residents demand stricter rules for 800-acre 1GW data center
items.dek: Opponents cite water-source loopholes and poll 82% support for recalling officials if the zoning ordinance fails to protect land and resources. The Planning Commission meets August 26 with no public agenda or project application yet.
items.findings: Proposed 800-plus-acre hyperscale AI data center per stopsolontownshipdatacenter.com | Consumers Energy reported in Q2 earnings meeting on July 28, 2026 that a 1 GW data center developer is still working through local zoning processes per opposition site posts | Draft zoning ordinance includes Special Land Use section allowing alternative water sources if "low impact" shown, per group calls to close loopholes | No agenda or draft 6 of ordinance released publicly ahead of Aug. 26 meeting per stopsolontownshipdatacenter.com posts | Next Planning Commission meeting is Wednesday, August 26 per opposition site
items.perspective: The commission has repeatedly delayed action on the ordinance amid opposition. Wednesday's meeting allows public comment on strengthening the rules, with the ordinance potentially advancing to the township board for adoption or referendum. The outcome ties directly to power demand, farmland conversion, and tax-base questions in West Michigan.
